summary: Ryushin Kitao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested in 2014 and 2026).
Ryushin Saito works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He held a professorship at Bukkyo University (attested 2015) and served on the faculty at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Ryushin Sudo (1929–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Taisho University (~1948–1952). He later served as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) studied at Ryukoku University (~1950–1954) and worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1974–1998).

Ryusho Hikata (1892–1991), a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1914–1917) under Junjirō Takakusu and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University (1950). He held posts at Kyushu University, Fukuoka Women's University, and the Japan Academy.

Ryuta Kikutani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held positions at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2020), and serves as an associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Ryutaro Tsuchida, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Marburg, where he was supervised by Wilhelm Rau. He was an assistant at Marburg (~1979–1983) and later professor and professor emeritus at Tokyo.

Takayoku Kimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Komazawa University (~1966–1970). He was a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1978), a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).
Ryuyu Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.
Ryuzan Nishimoto (1891–1974) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1916, he studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa.

Ryōmin Akizuki (1921–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1947). He later taught Makio Takemura and held a post at Saitama Medical University (~1972–1986).

Rüdiger Schmitt is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1958–1965) and served on the faculty at Saarland University (~1972–2004).
S. A. S. Sarma is an Indology scholar who held positions at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2004 and 2024.
S. Bhaskaran Nair is an Indologist who served at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute in roles including Deputy Director (attested 1974–1977, 1986) and General Editor (attested 1944, 1992).

S. D. Laddu (1926–2021) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He was a colleague at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1968) and editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).
S. Ghosh was active in Tibetology, serving in 1982 as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.
S. K. Maity is an Indology and history scholar who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1953–1956). He held a post at Jadavpur University from around 1958 to 1986.

S. K. Ramanatha Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He worked as temporary staff at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and was Junior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras until 1938.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) studied history at the University of Madras, where he later held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology (1914–1929). He also taught at Bengaluru City University and edited the Journal of Indian History (~1921–1946).

S. Kuppuswami Sastri (1880–1943), an Indologist and philosopher, studied at St. Peter's College and the University of Madras. He served as principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and as professor at Presidency College and Annamalai University.
